import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 598

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/598](https://www.erdosproblems.com/598)
-/

namespace Erdos598

open Cardinal

variable (m : Type*) [Infinite m]

/--
Let $\kappa = (2^{\aleph_0})^+$. This is the successor cardinal of the continuum.
-/
noncomputable def κ : Cardinal := Order.succ (2 ^ ℵ₀)

/--
**Erdős Problem 598:**
Let $m$ be an infinite cardinal and $\kappa$ be the successor cardinal of $2^{\aleph_0}$.
Can one colour the countable subsets of $m$ using $\kappa$ many colours so that every
$X \subseteq m$ with $|X| = \kappa$ contains subsets of all possible colours?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 5]
theorem erdos_598 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ c : { s : Set m // s.Countable } → κ.out,
    ∀ X : Set m, #X = κ →
    c '' { s : { sub : Set m // sub.Countable } | s.1 ⊆ X } = Set.univ := by
  sorry

end Erdos598

findings.description: The section variables `m` and `[Infinite m]` are quantified outside `answer(sorry) ↔`. Writing P(m) for the colouring-existence predicate, a fixed yes/no answer A therefore gives `∀ m [Infinite m], A ↔ P(m)`, whereas the source asks `A ↔ ∀ m [Infinite m], P(m)`. This distinction matters: P(ℕ) holds vacuously because ℵ₀ < κ, so a constant colouring suffices. Consequently the current answer template forces A to be true; `answer(False)` cannot express a negative answer witnessed by one failing infinite cardinal. In scratch Lean, I proved P(ℕ) and that the current template is equivalent to `A ∧ ∀ m [Infinite m], P(m)`, without using any sorry-backed result.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, “Some problems on finite and infinite graphs,” Contemporary Mathematics 65 (1987), Problem 8, pp. 225–226: “Is it true that for every infinite m one can color the countable subset[s] of m by (2^{ℵ₀})⁺ colors so that every subset of size (2^{ℵ₀})⁺ gets subsets of all the colors?” https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-28.pdf
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the outer `variable (m : Type*) [Infinite m]` declaration and put `∀ (m : Type u) [Infinite m],` immediately after `answer(sorry) ↔`, declaring `universe u`. Keep the colouring-existence predicate inside that quantifier.

reformulations.difference: Independently of the answer-scope defect, `Set.Countable` includes finite and empty subsets. If the source's “countable subsets” is interpreted as countably infinite subsets, this enlarges the colouring domain but does not change colouring existence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An infinite-subset colouring extends arbitrarily to finite subsets. Conversely, well-order m. For an infinite countable T of order type ω^(α+1), let F(T) be its first α elements; set F(T)=∅ on other order types. Given any κ-sized X, choose Y⊆X of order type κ. Since κ is uncountable regular, every countable s⊆Y is bounded. If s has order type α, append above s a tail of order type ω^(α+1), obtaining T⊆Y with F(T)=s. Thus composing an at-most-countable-subset colouring with F realizes every colour on countably infinite subsets of every κ-sized X.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Some problems on finite and infinite graphs, Contemporary Mathematics 65 (1987), 223–228, especially Problem 8, pp. 225–226: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1987-28.pdf
Local Mathlib sources: Data/Set/Countable.lean and SetTheory/Cardinal/{Defs,Order,Continuum,Regular}.lean; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean.

The current community database lists problem 598 as open; no status discrepancy was established. The definition κ, palette cardinality, universe lifting, image/surjectivity condition, and boundary cases were checked. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully, and its semantic and scope-test proofs do not depend on sorryAx. No repository files were edited.

not_demonstrated.reason: The exact imported type has answer(sorry) elaborated to True and remains the universal positive colouring assertion. The short proof for m = ℕ proves only a legitimate special case, not the whole declaration. Refuting the False-filled answer template would change the statement and therefore would not satisfy the as-stated requirement.

submission.summary: No trivial_proof.lean was created. A separate exact_type_check.lean compiled without errors or sorry warnings and proved that the imported type is equivalent to the universal colouring assertion; this is not a proof or disproof of that assertion.
submission.gave_up_reason: The reported answer-scope concern affects how a negative answer would be represented, but does not yield a short, honest proof or disproof of the declaration as currently elaborated.

submission.summary: Moved `∀ (m : Type u) [Infinite m]` inside `answer(sorry) ↔` and removed the outer section parameters. Updated the docstring to make the universal question explicit. The file compiles with only the expected `sorry` warning.
